output.myth: A boat went out past the Leeward rocks when Tavo the Gale came down on her like a dropped net. Her name was painted on the bow in red ochre. The sea took the ochre first, then the wood, so when the shore-folk found her ribs nobody could say what she had been called. They scraped what was left of the letters from the hull and kept the flakes in a cloth. Her lantern did not go out. It went up the mast of the sky and hangs there, a light with no name. The old ones say it is searching for one. Kael the Netter casts for it every night and hauls up only weed. Hesk keeps count of it and will not write it down until someone gives it a name. So if you see a lamp low in the south, do not call it lost. Say the name your mother gave you, and let the wind carry it.
output.verse:
A lamp with no name
The sea took the ochre first
It hunts for its name
